classes.name: Statins
classes.description: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors: atorvastatin (Lipitor), rosuvastatin (Crestor, Ezallor), simvastatin (Zocor), pravastatin, lovastatin (Altoprev), pitavastatin (Livalo, Zypitamag), fluvastatin, and statin combinations (Vytorin, Roszet).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill that lowers LDL cholesterol.

classes.name: Ezetimibe & other non-statin oral agents
classes.description: Non-statin oral LDL-lowering agents: ezetimibe (Zetia), bempedoic acid (Nexletol) and bempedoic acid/ezetimibe (Nexlizet).
classes.plainDescription: A cholesterol pill used with or instead of a statin.

classes.name: PCSK9 inhibitors & siRNA
classes.description: Injectable PCSK9-pathway agents: evolocumab (Repatha), alirocumab (Praluent), inclisiran (Leqvio).
classes.plainDescription: An injection every 2 weeks to 6 months that strongly lowers LDL cholesterol.

preferredAgent.sig: 1 tablet by mouth once daily (standard label dosing; not stated in PDL)

records.verificationNote: Read FL Medicaid PDL p.51 (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors). Preferred pick: generic atorvastatin 40 mg, PA column No, age 0+ (judgment: the most commonly prescribed statin on the list). Sig is standard label dosing; the PDL prints no sig. Pitavastatin, fluvastatin, Altoprev, Vytorin and Roszet are not on the PDL and are recorded as PA required (not on the PDL). Ezallor is not listed. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: removed 5 absence-only PA/nonformulary entries (Livalo / Zypitamag (pitavastatin), Fluvastatin (generic), Altoprev (lovastatin ER), Vytorin (ezetimibe/simvastatin), Roszet (rosuvastatin/ezetimibe)): the PDL (pp.1-2 definitions) says nothing about non-listed drugs requiring PA, so absence is not evidence]

records.verificationNote: Read FL Medicaid PDL p.53 (PCSK9 inhibitors). All three PCSK9-pathway agents are Auto PA: Repatha (min age 10), Praluent (min age 8), Leqvio (min age 12).
